findings.title: Add/remove members require group_id the route never sets
findings.body: add_members and remove_member (line 85) load the group with params.require(:group_id). The new routes in config/routes.rb are bare put/delete "members" inside resources :groups, which are member routes on /admin/groups/:id/members. That segment is params[:id], the same param this controller already uses for update and destroy. Elsewhere in routes.rb a non-default name is written into the path (delete "groups/:group_id"); these member routes do not do that, so group_id is never populated. The Ember client only interpolates the id into the path and posts usernames or user_id, not group_id. require(:group_id) raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove returns 400. Controller specs stay green because they pass group_id directly and never hit the router. Read params[:id], matching update/destroy.

findings.title: Members action requires group_id but the route sets id
findings.body: The rewritten members action still calls find_group(:group_id), and find_group does params.require on that key. The route is get "members" inside resources :groups, i.e. GET /groups/:id/members, so the group name arrives in params[:id]. show in this same controller correctly uses find_group(:id); posts and counts have the same mismatch. Group#findMembers requests /groups/:name/members.json and only sends limit and offset, not group_id. The action 400s before it can return the new members/meta payload, so both the admin member list and the public members page stay empty. Use find_group(:id).

findings.title: remove_member passes an integer to association delete
findings.body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with a raw integer. On Rails 4, CollectionAssociation#delete type-checks its arguments and raises ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch (User expected, got Fixnum) instead of deleting the group_users join row. Once the group_id param bug is fixed, removing a member still 500s and the user stays in the group. The new spec expects 200 and a user count of 0, so it fails if run. Load the user and call group.remove(user), which is what the previous membership update path used, or pass a User record to delete.

findings.title: Public members page cannot show past the first 50 users
findings.body: The public members route only calls model.findMembers() once, and Group#findMembers always sends limit 50 (the model default). groups/members.hbs has no pager and does not show the new meta.total. GroupsController#members now applies that limit to every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned every member and automatic groups defaulted to 200. Anyone opening a group with more than 50 members sees a silently truncated list and has no way to load the rest. The admin screen has next/previous; this page does not. Either paginate here or request a limit large enough to preserve the old full list.

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when count divides evenly
findings.body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (50, 100, and so on) that is an extra page: 50 members with limit 50 displays 1/2 and leaves Next enabled. next() then sets offset to user_count, findMembers returns no rows, and the admin lands on a blank member page. Math.ceil(user_count / limit) is the right count (0 stays 0).

findings.title: Create ignores alias_level the form submits
findings.body: create sets name and visible but never alias_level. The new-group form shows the alias-level combo outside the id check, and Group#asJSON posts alias_level on create. The column stays at the default 0 (nobody can mention the group). The client only copies resp.basic_group.id back onto the model, so the UI keeps the level the admin chose and then transitions to the group page. They have no reason to hit Save again; after a reload the mention permission has reverted. update does persist alias_level. The create spec only checks that the name is stripped.

findings.title: Member reloads use the unsaved group name
findings.body: findMembers requests /groups/ plus this.get('name') plus /members.json. In the admin form the name text field is two-way bound to that same property, and pagination, add, and remove all call findMembers before Save. An edited but unsaved name is sent to the server. If it matches no group the reload 404s and the member list fails with no error UI (next/previous have already moved offset). If it matches a different group, that group's members are shown on this group's screen while add/remove still target this group's numeric id, so the admin can change the wrong memberships. Fetch with the persisted name, not the in-progress field.

findings.title: Enter in the group form activates Add instead of Save
findings.body: The admin group editor is now wrapped in a form, but Add, Save, and Delete are button elements with no type attribute, so they default to submit. On an existing non-automatic group the first submit button is Add. Pressing Enter in the name field (or the user selector) activates Add rather than Save: members are added, or addMembers returns immediately because the username box is empty, and the name, visibility, and alias level are not saved. Delete is also a submit button. Set type="button" on these action buttons. If the action helper does not preventDefault, the browser will also GET-submit the form to the current URL and reload the page, dropping unsaved edits.

findings.title: Spaced usernames are skipped and add still succeeds
findings.body: add_members splits the usernames string on commas and calls User.find_by_username on each token without stripping. A space after a comma, which is normal when typing into the selector ("alice, bob"), does not match username_lower, so that user is not added. Unknown names are skipped the same way. If group.save then succeeds, the action still renders success_json even when nobody was added. The admin UI reloads the current page and does not clear the input (the controller has a TODO for that), so the add looks successful. Strip each username and report names that did not match instead of returning success unconditionally.

findings.title: Add/remove failures are silent and desync the pager
findings.body: addMembers and removeMember (line 56) ignore the promises returned by the model. Those model methods only call findMembers on success and have no failure path. save and destroy in this same controller show a bootbox alert. A 400, 422 from an automatic group, or 500 therefore leaves the list unchanged with no message, so the admin cannot tell a failure from a no-op. next and previous also write offset before findMembers resolves, so a failed page load leaves the pager on a page whose members were never fetched. Overlapping findMembers responses are applied unconditionally, so a slower earlier page can overwrite a newer one.

findings.title: Members limit and offset are unbounded
findings.body: limit and offset come from the query string with only to_i and no range check. The endpoint is available to anyone who can see the group. limit=1000000 loads and serializes every member of a large automatic group such as trust_level_0 in one response, which is a straightforward DoS. offset=-1 or limit=-1 makes PostgreSQL reject the statement (OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative) and the action returns 500. Clamp offset to >= 0 and cap limit to a small maximum; the UI only requests 50.

findings.title: Members JSON shape and default size break existing clients
findings.body: GET /groups/:name/members.json used to return a top-level JSON array of users (the previous client called result.map on it). It now returns an object with members and meta. When limit is omitted the action also returns at most 50 rows instead of the full roster for custom groups or the previous default of 200 for automatic groups. In-repo callers in this PR were updated, but external API clients, scripts, and plugins that still expect an array will throw or stop listing members, and callers that omitted limit silently lose everyone past 50. There is no version flag or fallback to the old shape.

findings.title: Membership specs bypass routing and skip the public members API
findings.body: The new add_members and remove_member examples invoke the actions with group_id in the params hash. That never loads config/routes.rb, so they pass even when PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members does not set group_id, which is the URL the Ember client uses. The automatic-group remove example uses xhr :put while the route is DELETE. Nothing in this PR covers GroupsController#members: the switch from a JSON array to {members, meta}, the new default limit of 50, or invalid limit/offset. Those are the paths the admin pager and the public members page depend on, and they can be broken while this spec stays green.
